26 In an experiment to demonstrate a stationary wave, two microwave transmitters, emitting waves
of wavelength 4 cm, are set facing each other, as shown.

A detector is moved along a straight line between the transmitters. It detects positions of
maximum and minimum signal. The detector is a distance d from the left-hand transmitter.
Assume that both transmitters are at antinodes of the stationary wave.
Which row gives a value of d for a maximum and for a minimum?

hints: Notice the wavelength is $4 \text{ cm}$ and the left-hand transmitter at $d = 0$ is assumed to be an antinode where the signal is maximum.
Recall antinodes are spaced by $\lambda/2 = 2 \text{ cm}$ and nodes lie half-way between them, at $\lambda/4 = 1 \text{ cm}$ from an antinode.
Check which of 46, 47, 48, 49 cm is a whole number of $2 \text{ cm}$ steps from 0 and which is $1 \text{ cm}$ away from such a position.
walkthrough: The two opposite $4 \text{ cm}$ waves superpose to form a stationary wave with maximum signal at antinodes and minimum signal at nodes.
The left transmitter is given as an antinode, so take $d = 0$ as an antinode.
Antinode to next antinode distance is $\lambda/2 = 4/2 = 2 \text{ cm}$, so maxima occur at $d = 0, 2, 4, ...$ cm, i.e. all even numbers of cm.
Nodes are midway between antinodes, a distance $\lambda/4 = 1 \text{ cm}$ from an antinode, so minima occur at $d = 1, 3, 5, ...$ cm, i.e. all odd numbers of cm.
Hence $d = 48 \text{ cm} = 24 \times 2 \text{ cm}$ is an antinode and gives a maximum, while $d = 47 \text{ cm}$ is $1 \text{ cm}$ from 48 cm and gives a minimum.

A.explanation: 46 cm is $23 \times \lambda/2$ from an antinode so it is a node, not a maximum, and 48 cm is an antinode, not a minimum.

B.explanation: 47 cm is an odd multiple of $1 \text{ cm}$ from the transmitter antinode so it is a node and gives a minimum, not a maximum.

C.explanation: 48 cm is $24 \times 2 \text{ cm}$ from the antinode so it is an antinode maximum, and 47 cm is half-way between antinodes so it is a node minimum.

D.explanation: 49 cm is an odd number of cm from the transmitter antinode so it is a node and gives a minimum, not a maximum.
